evidence: Both 2002 articles, The Conservatives and British Society (1996), and The Flyer (2008) belong to Martin Francis's documented bibliography. The RAF Museum biography also connects The Flyer with his research on prime ministers' emotions and male domesticity.

a combines John Clare Moore's Innocent III scholarship with John Hammond Moore's coauthored 1968 Senator John Tyler Morgan article and other namesakes' work. LC n99019595 identifies John Clare Moore (1933-); n50004293 identifies John Hammond Moore (born 1924), author of b's Southern-history books: distinct people.

a mixes Steven Hahn's Roots of Southern Populism and A Nation Under Our Feet with Steven C. Hahn's 2015 Pocahontas of Georgia article, which belongs with b's Mary Musgrove biography. LC n82111016 (Steven, born 1951) and n2003120078 (Steven C., born 1968, St. Olaf) describe distinct historians.

a mixes David Levering Lewis's King, Harlem and Du Bois books with David Rich Lewis's Native American environmental scholarship. The Smithsonian catalogue credits a's Skull Valley Goshutes chapter to David Rich Lewis, coeditor of b's 2007 book. LC n50049263 and n93102139 describe these distinct historians.

a's The Self and Its Pleasures and Holocaust books are Carolyn Janice Dean's modern European history; b's Inka Bodies and A Culture of Stone are Carolyn Dean's Andean art history. LC n92059954 (born 1960) and n99000049 (born 1957) identify distinct women, corroborated by Yale and UC Santa Cruz faculty biographies.

Evolution and Society, A Liberal Descent and A History of Histories belong to intellectual historian John Wyon Burrow. Sir Gawain, Ricardian Poetry and the Hoccleve studies belong to medieval literary scholar John Anthony Burrow. LC n50035230 and n79071276 identify distinct people, born 1935 and 1932 respectively.

a combines David Linley Potter's Renaissance France books with Roman-history work, including Measuring the Power of the Roman Empire, belonging to David Stone Potter's career represented by b. LC n92037298 identifies the Kent French historian (born 1948); n90645101 identifies the Michigan classicist (born 1957): distinct people.

a chiefly contains John K. Walton's British leisure history but also the 1906 Oregon university article, credited to J. J. Walton, decades before John K.'s birth. b is sociologist John Walton, author of Reluctant Rebels and Western Times and Water Wars. LC n78097321 (born 1948) and n50026469 (born 1937) identify distinct people.

a is José Angel Hernández, born 1969, whose 2008 Chicago dissertation became Mexican American Colonization (2012). b is José Hernández (1834-1886), the Argentine author of Martín Fierro; later dates are editions of his works. LC n2012007649 and n79124916 describe different people separated by generations.

Lyndal Roper's Holy Household, Witch Craze and Oedipus and the Devil concern Reformation Germany, gender and witchcraft. Louis H. Roper's Conceiving Carolina, English Empire in America and Advancing Empire concern English Atlantic colonization. LC n86079409 and n2003049938 identify distinct historians, at Oxford and SUNY New Paltz respectively.

a's Venetian Inquisition article fits John Jeffries Martin's Venice's Hidden Enemies, but its 1999 consumption-economy article and 2001 Authoritarian Personality article are credited to sociologist John Levi Martin. Thus a combines at least two authors and cannot be merged wholesale with b's Renaissance historian.

a is Scott MacKenzie (born 1967), Queen's film scholar responsible for Cinema and Nation, Screening Québec and Film Manifestos. b is Simon Paul MacKenzie (born 1961), South Carolina military historian responsible for Politics and Military Morale, The Home Guard and The Colditz Myth. LC n00035850 and n91062293 describe distinct people despite both writing about film.

a combines Brian Jeffery Young's Quebec railway, Cartier and civil-code books with the 2012 John Jortin article, explicitly credited to B. W. Young of Christ Church, Oxford. That article belongs with b's British intellectual history. LC n78046553 (Brian J., born 1940) and n97092147 (Brian Walter, born 1963) describe distinct historians.

a chiefly represents Cambridge international historian David Reynolds, but its Science Society of China title is catalogued under David C. Reynolds, a separate author. b's Whitman, Lippard and American Renaissance books are David S. Reynolds's literary history. LC n81100445 (born 1952) and n80103048 (born 1948) identify distinct people; a also contains third-author contamination.

a mixes James Gow's Yugoslav war and war-crimes books with James Iain Gow's Quebec scholarship: the 1990 administration article is explicitly credited to James Iain Gow, matching b's public-administration books. LC n91066098 identifies the King's College London security scholar; n86017306 identifies the Université de Montréal scholar (born 1934): distinct people.
